## The rule

A red candidate becomes a **frozen candidate** once the gate records its exact commit and opens the repair queue. That candidate is the only candidate that may advance until it is green or an explicitly bounded escape retires it.

The queue's identity is two-part:

- `candidate` is the commit that first failed the gate and is immutable for the queue entry.
- `repairHead` is the exact head that fixes move forward from. It starts at `candidate`, and every accepted repair must be a descendant of the previous `repairHead`.

Do not cut a new candidate from the moving tip, cherry-pick a mixed sweep commit, or start a broad sweep while this queue is active. A new tip cut re-admits work that the frozen candidate has not proved and turns one convergence problem back into an unbounded candidate stream.

This is the convergence invariant recorded by `converge-frozen-candidate-by-fix-only-admission-2026-08-27#P-010` (D-001, D-002, D-003, D-004, and D-007).

## Why freezing matters

Selection-based recovery cannot make progress when each red result is replaced by another tip cut: the next candidate includes new, unrelated changes before the repair for the previous candidate can be judged. The gate then compares different objects on every run, and a passing repair may never be the object that gets verified.

Freezing gives the gate one stable object and a monotone sequence of repair heads:

```text
candidate C  --> repairHead C --> repairHead R1 --> repairHead R2 --> green
                  (same queue; forward descendants only)
```

The green-checkpoint suite must judge the exact head named by the queue. Never move `repairHead` while a verification is running (D-004), and stop the loop if a round adds failures instead of shrinking them (D-005).

## The only admission path

1. **Select and persist once.** The gate records `candidate`, `base`, `repairHead`, the isolated `worktreePath`, and the failing tests before dispatching a fixer. A later checkpoint reads that durable queue instead of selecting a fresh tip.
2. **Repair in isolation.** The fixer works only in the named repair worktree, starting at the current `repairHead`. It reproduces the failure, makes the smallest source edit, runs focused tests, and advances the worktree head forward. It must not move `main`, push, or use the shared staging checkout as its authoring tree.
3. **Finalize as a forward commit.** Finalization may commit dirty files in the repair worktree, but the resulting head is accepted only when the old `repairHead` is an ancestor. A non-forward move is a hard stop: diagnose the worktree rather than replacing the queue with a new candidate.
4. **Verify the exact repair head.** Run the named focused/full verification against that repair head. The candidate SHA in the run record, logs, and verdict must agree with the queue. If the head changes, the result is inconclusive and must not promote anything.
5. **Admit by plumbing, after verification.** The repair head is not itself the release ref. The admission bridge names the source commit and proves that every source-only path is represented identically on the current staging tree (mode, object, deletion, or gitlink); only then may it record contained ancestry without changing unrelated staging content. The allowlist/diff-tree check is the proof that no foreign sweep file entered (D-002/P-003). A mismatch is a no-op or hold, never a best-effort merge.
6. **Promote the proven tree.** Confirm the tested repair is present on staging, then let the normal green-checkpoint promotion advance the release ref. If the exact patch is absent or staging diverged, retain the queue and diagnose; do not re-cut at tip to make the mismatch disappear.

`git add -A` in the shared checkout is not an admission mechanism. It can collect peer or sweep work that was never part of the frozen candidate. The repair worktree authors; plumbing admits.

## What a repair agent should do

A cold or resumed fixer receiving `frozenCandidate`, `repairHead`, and `repairWorktree` should:

- treat those values as the authoritative scope and work from the named worktree;
- read the newest gate log, reproduce every named failure, and classify regression versus flake before changing code;
- keep edits narrow, run focused tests, and apply the identical source edits to canonical staging under its normal file locks;
- leave commits and pushes to the gate/git-sync machinery; and
- exit after focused verification so the serialized checkpoint can finalize and run the one authoritative full verdict.

If the dispatch context is missing its repair worktree or the worktree cannot reproduce the named candidate, stop with an explicit diagnosis. Do not silently fall back to staging or tip.

## Exhaustion and the bounded exception

The default queue limits are fail-closed: attempts or wall-clock exhaustion holds the same candidate, with no automatic tip cut. This preserves the invariant even when automation is unhealthy.

The code has an explicit, owner-ratified escape hatch, `maxCandidateEscapes`. It is **zero by default**. A nonzero value permits only that many recorded `recut-at-tip` escapes after exhaustion; each escape must be observable, bounded, and treated as retirement of the exhausted queue, not as ordinary convergence. Raising the bound is a Phase-2 policy change, not a fixer shortcut.

## Checklist before declaring progress

- [ ] The queue's `candidate` and current `repairHead` are read from durable metadata.
- [ ] The repair head is a descendant of the prior head and the verification targets that exact SHA.
- [ ] The fixer authored in the isolated repair worktree; no shared-tree sweep or tip recut was used.
- [ ] Every changed path is in the intended allowlist and passes the diff-tree/tree-entry proof.
- [ ] Staging contains the verified repair before promotion.
- [ ] A non-shrinking round, staging mismatch, moving head, or exhausted budget is held and diagnosed rather than hidden by a new candidate.

The sources of truth are `frozen-candidate-repair-queue.ts` for queue policy, `green-checkpoint.ts` for serialization and verification, `release-actions.ts` for fixer dispatch/finalization, and `run-git-sync.ts` for the contained ancestry bridge.
